steps.path: Marketplace → Connect your stuff → Google Workspace
steps.headline: Three ways to line up the integration's tile, name, description and buttons. Which looks right?
steps.notice: All keep the big coloured tile. 'One row' is how the Account profile card and every settings row line up, so it is my pick by the guide.

variants.label: One row
variants.summary: Tile, then name and description, then Uninstall and Connect — all centred on one line. The shortest card.

variants.label: Tile centred
variants.summary: The tile sits centred beside the name and description; the buttons get their own line at the right.

variants.label: Round 3
variants.summary: The tile beside the name only; the description runs under both, buttons below.

steps.path: Any theme page → the top card on the right (here: Meadow Mist)
steps.headline: Three ways to fit the theme's chips in the narrow right column. Which looks better?
steps.notice: In all three the heart, star and share are back on the name's line, and the name only ever wraps between words.

variants.label: Chips wrap
variants.summary: Author, downloads and likes as chips, allowed onto a second line instead of fading.

variants.label: A facts line
variants.summary: No chips: 'by claude · 1,240 downloads · 88 likes' as one quiet line under the buttons.
variants.risk: Different from every other detail page, which keeps a chip row.

variants.label: Fewer chips
variants.summary: Just the author and the likes, which fit on one line; downloads is dropped here.
variants.risk: The download count no longer shows on theme pages.

steps.path: Any theme page → the heart at the top of the top card
steps.headline: The like button is now just a heart; its count is the '88 likes' chip, which changes the moment you click.
steps.changed: The other like-button styles are removed. When you like or unlike, the chip's number goes up or down at once, before the server answers, and goes back if it fails.
steps.notice: The heart fills with the accent colour when liked, like the star.
